name: Chuck Berry
hook: The guitarist and songwriter whose Chess singles were the first records the Beatles and the Rolling Stones learned to play.
blurb: Chuck Berry was born in St. Louis in 1926. In May 1955 he went to Chicago, met Muddy Waters, and Muddy told him to go and see Leonard Chess. Chess liked Berry's fast version of an old country fiddle tune, 'Ida Red', which became 'Maybellene', recorded on 21 May 1955. It went to number one on the R&B chart and sold over a million copies. That a Black guitarist's breakthrough was a reworked country song, pushed by a blues label, says a lot about how mixed the sources of rock and roll were. 'Roll Over Beethoven' (1956), 'Rock and Roll Music' (1957) and 'Johnny B. Goode' (1958) followed: songs about cars, school and dancing, with a sharp, ringing guitar part at the start, later covered by the Beatles and the Rolling Stones. In December 1959 he was arrested under the Mann Act for taking a 14-year-old girl across state lines, and he served about eighteen months in federal prison, from February 1962 to October 1963, the same period when British bands were learning his songs. He died in 2017.
